title: Indian Overseas Bank Profit Jumps 56% as It Targets $500 Million Fundraise
excerpt: IOB posted Q2 net profit of Rs 1,912 crore on 26% growth in net interest income, improved NPAs to 1.19%, and said $250 million of its planned $500 million overseas borrowing is already finalised.
body:
• Indian Overseas Bank reported standalone net profit of Rs 1,912 crore for Q2 FY27, up 56% year on year from Rs 1,226 crore, helped by higher interest income and a lower tax outgo.
  • Net interest income rose 26% to Rs 3,867 crore, operating profit rose 26% to Rs 3,016 crore, and gross NPA improved to 1.19% from 1.83% a year earlier.
  • The bank is targeting $500 million through the RBI's external commercial borrowing window by December, with about $250 million already finalised.
  • For investors, IOB shares ended at Rs 30.38 on the NSE, up almost 6% on the results day; advances grew 24.35% and deposits 20% year on year.

Indian Overseas Bank reported a 56% jump in net profit to Rs 1,912 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, and said it is targeting a $500 million fundraise by December. The public sector lender's profit rose from Rs 1,226 crore in the same quarter last year, buoyed by higher interest income, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

Interest income rose 17% to Rs 9,201 crore in the September quarter, from Rs 7,849 crore a year earlier. Net interest income increased 26% year on year to Rs 3,867 crore, and operating profit also increased 26% to Rs 3,016 crore. The bank's domestic net interest margin rose 14 basis points year on year to 3.49%.

Credit growth drives the quarter

Total business grew with advances up 24.35% to Rs 3,45,650 crore and deposits up 20% year on year to Rs 4,07,428 crore. Growth came from the retail, agriculture and MSME portfolio: retail credit was up 33.77%, agriculture up 47.31%, largely on agri jewel loans, and MSME credit up 13.8%.

"Our internal aspiration and mandate is that every year, net profit on a year-on-year basis should grow by a minimum of 25-30 per cent. If you look at our last 10 quarters, you will find this consistency."

— Ajay Kumar Srivastava, Managing Director & CEO, Indian Overseas Bank

Srivastava attributed the performance to strong credit expansion and the bank's ability to manage funding costs, and to faster processing and decentralised sourcing through branches and loan processing centres. He said he does not anticipate stress in the jewel loan category.

On deposits, the bank mobilised around Rs 11,000 crore, or $1.2 billion, in FCNR(B) deposits under a special window, and said the entire amount had been suitably deployed. Even without that mobilisation, deposits grew 17%, the managing director said.

Asset quality and provisions

Asset quality continued to improve. The gross NPA ratio fell 64 basis points year on year to 1.19%, and the net NPA ratio fell 12 basis points to 0.16%, primarily on steady recoveries, according to The Hindu BusinessLine's detailed results coverage.

On the expected credit loss framework, IOB said it had already made around Rs 2,700 crore in provisions, which management expects to cover the anticipated requirement, and will continue building buffers over the next two quarters. Other income fell 43% sequentially because the bank had earned around Rs 900 crore from priority sector lending certificates in the first quarter, which did not recur in the second quarter.

Consolidated figures filed with the exchanges put total income at Rs 10,427.88 crore for the September quarter, up 13.1% year on year, according to a summary of the exchange filings reported by Angel One.

The $500 million fundraise

IOB is targeting $500 million in fundraising through the Reserve Bank of India's external commercial borrowing window by December. Around $250 million has been finalised, with the remaining amount under discussion with banks and agencies.

"Overall, $500 million by December is what we are targeting. Around $250 million has already been finalised, and for the balance $250 million, we are in discussions with banks and agencies."

— Ajay Kumar Srivastava, Managing Director & CEO, Indian Overseas Bank

What investors should watch

Shares of IOB ended the trading day at Rs 30.38, up almost 6% on the NSE, according to BusinessLine. For diaspora investors holding Indian bank stocks through NRE or other permitted routes, the test now is whether credit growth near 24%, a 1.19% gross NPA ratio and the planned overseas borrowing can be sustained without fresh stress in jewel loans or a rise in credit costs as the expected credit loss buffers are built.

The bank also said it had benchmarked its cybersecurity systems against industry practices and engaged PwC to identify gaps and recommend improvements, describing the work as a continuous process requiring round-the-clock monitoring.
